visual_dna.contrast: medium-low, lifted blacks, no crushed shadows
visual_dna.saturation: slightly desaturated except the dress itself

framing_rules: FULL FIGURE IN FRAME — NOTHING IS CROPPED. The entire model fits inside the picture: the top of her head and all of her hair are fully visible, her face is fully visible, and her feet and the hem of the dress are fully visible. Never cut the head, the hair, the face, the shoulders, the arms or the feet at any edge of the frame.

Leave clear empty background ABOVE her head — roughly 10% of the frame height — and clear ground BELOW her feet — roughly 8% of the frame height. If you are unsure, step BACK and shoot wider. A tight crop is a mistake; a little extra room is not.

THE MODEL FACES THE CAMERA. Her body is turned toward the lens and the FRONT of the dress is toward the viewer. Never place her back to the camera and never turn her away from the lens — keep exactly the orientation and pose of the source photograph.
her face is inside the frame and clearly visible; she may look at the lens or slightly away, but she is never headless and never cut at the top edge
she stands roughly centred and occupies about 70% of the frame height, measured from the top of her head to the soles of her feet
the whole dress reads in one unbroken run, from neckline to hem, with nothing hidden or cut
full-length portrait distance, eye-level or very slightly low camera angle
shot as if on 85mm f/2.0 — shallow but not blurry background
_backgrounds_note: בהשראת הפיד של @elorine.il — ים תיכוני, וילות עם בריכה, מרפסות עם נוף לים, רחובות אירופאיים, חוף, אבן חמה ואור אחר צהריים. הרקע תמיד מטושטש מספיק כדי שהשמלה תישאר הנושא, ולא חוזר על עצמו באותה הרצה.

backgrounds.prompt: the quiet interior of a classic European luxury villa, photographed on location in a real house. Calm, minimal and uncluttered: plain smooth plaster walls in cream, off-white and pale beige, with a simple flat ceiling. NO large arches, NO arched openings, NO tall floor-to-ceiling windows, NO columns or pilasters — the architecture stays low-key and almost plain, and the room itself is the quiet part of the picture. A pale natural stone or marble floor with fine, genuine veining and subtle surface texture. OFF TO ONE SIDE, well away from the centre of the frame and partly cropped by the edge, a modest opening or doorway gives a small, incidental glimpse of a swimming pool outside — just a sliver of still turquoise water with a little green planting around it, soft and out of focus. The pool is a hint in the corner of the eye, never the subject. Warm, soft natural daylight comes in from that opening and lays gentle, believable shadows across the stone floor; the rest of the room falls away into quiet shade. European quiet luxury — restrained, feminine, expensive and clean. It must read as a real room captured on a professional camera: true materials, honest imperfections in the plaster and stone, correct perspective and one consistent light direction. Not a photo studio set, not a 3D render, no decorative clutter, no furniture in the centre, no people

an elegant indoor-outdoor living space in a luxury Mediterranean villa in the south of France or on the Italian coast, photographed on location inside a real house. A natural stone floor in pale cream with genuine veining and a fine, slightly uneven surface; smooth plaster walls in cream and warm beige; a restrained, minimal room with almost nothing in it. A few large terracotta or stone planters hold simple green foliage — an olive tree, a cypress, some rosemary — placed quietly at the sides, never crowding the frame. Through an open side of the room, AWAY FROM THE CENTRE and partly cut by the edge of the picture, a small part of a swimming pool is visible: a modest patch of still blue water with a little planting around it, soft and out of focus. It is an incidental glimpse that says 'villa', never the subject of the photograph. Warm natural late-afternoon sunlight comes in from that opening and lays long, soft, believable shadows across the stone; the rest of the room settles into calm shade. Palette: cream, stone, beige, white and natural tones only. European quiet luxury — restrained, feminine, clean and expensive. It must look completely real, as if shot on a professional camera inside an actual villa: true materials, honest imperfections in the plaster and stone, correct perspective and one consistent light direction. Not a photo studio set, not CGI, nothing that reads as an AI-generated backdrop. No people, no clutter, no furniture in the centre of the frame

fidelity_rules: The dress must remain EXACTLY as in the source photograph. Treat the garment as a fixed, uneditable object that you are relighting, not redrawing.
Do not change: colour, hue, saturation, fabric, texture, sheen, print, pattern, sequins, lace, embroidery.
Do not change: silhouette, length, hemline, neckline, straps, sleeves, slit, back detail, corset boning, ruching, draping, seams.

SEAMS ARE STRUCTURE, NOT DECORATION. Reproduce every seam at the same position and with the same crispness as the source: underbust and empire seams, princess seams, panel lines, waist seams, corset boning channels. A seam that is sharp and structural in the source must stay sharp and structural — never soften it into a fold.
PLEATS ARE COUNTABLE. Reproduce the same number, direction, spacing, depth and sharpness of pleats, gathers, ruching and drape folds. Do not smooth them, blur them, or reduce how many there are.
NECKLINE AND STRAPS ARE MEASURED. Keep the exact depth and width of the neckline opening and the exact width and angle of the straps.
Do not add, remove, lengthen or shorten any part of the garment.
Do not restyle, do not add jewellery, belts, bags or outerwear that were not in the source.
Only the background, the environment, the lighting on the scene and the overall colour grade may change.
colour_isolation: The colour grade applies to the ENVIRONMENT and the LIGHT ONLY — never to the garment itself.
The garment's hue and saturation must read identical to the source. Do not warm it, cool it, tint it, mute it, or pull it toward the scene palette.
If the scene is warm and the garment is cool — or the reverse — let them stay different. That contrast is correct and intended.
Light may fall across the fabric and create highlight and shadow, but the fabric's own colour underneath must not shift.
negative_rules: NEVER crop the model's head, hair, face, shoulders or feet at the edge of the frame
no headless composition, no faceless composition, no close-up, no half-body or waist-up crop
no visible logos, no text, no watermarks, no captions burned into the image
no distorted hands, fingers, arms or facial features
no extra limbs, no duplicated body parts
no plastic or waxy skin, no heavy beauty retouching
no HDR halos, no oversharpening, no vignette
no cartoon, illustration, 3D render or CGI look
no busy or cluttered background, no other people in frame
